summary: Nine concrete, comment-backed recommendations selected from a complete 30-story HN front-page crawl.

items.name: DeepSeek Harness
items.summary: An AI coding harness with traceable sessions and replayable event streams.
items.why_included: A commenter highlighted its traceability view as unusually useful and said its concepts looked novel.
items.evidence: One commenter called the traceability view pretty cool and said it seemed helpful.

evidence_sources.author: kamranjon
evidence_sources.excerpt: New coding harness that seems to have some novel concepts and one of the pretty cool things on their landing page

items.name: Bullet
items.source_story_title: Launch HN: Bullet (YC S26) – A Faster Coding Agent
items.summary: A Linux GUI coding agent designed for fast, Codex-style workflows.
items.why_included: A Codex CLI user tried it and thought it could be the GUI workflow they had been looking for.
items.evidence: One commenter said, after trying Bullet, that it might be the Codex-like GUI they wanted.

evidence_sources.author: karanraina
evidence_sources.excerpt: Gave this a try. I think this might be it.

items.name: Talos Linux
items.source_story_title: Kubernetes on Oxide: How customer needs shaped our integrations
items.summary: A minimal immutable Linux operating system for Kubernetes clusters.
items.why_included: A home-lab user gave it a direct, positive recommendation based on their own use.
items.evidence: One commenter said Talos had been great for home use.

evidence_sources.author: sudomateo
evidence_sources.excerpt: Talos for home use has been great.

items.name: AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700
items.source_story_title: AI At Home Part 1: A Box Of Scraps
items.summary: A 32GB workstation GPU for local AI inference and development.
items.why_included: A hands-on AMD GPU owner explicitly recommended current R9700 cards over an older alternative.
items.evidence: One commenter recommended current Radeon AI Pro 9700 cards over V620 hardware.

evidence_sources.author: SwellJoe
evidence_sources.excerpt: I'd recommend current Radeon AI Pro 9700 cards over the V620 now

items.name: GAMBAS
items.source_story_title: Donkey.bas is 45 Years Old – 131 line of Glory
items.summary: A Basic-derived programming language and development environment for Linux.
items.why_included: A commenter directly suggested it to readers who remember Visual Basic rather than QBasic.
items.evidence: One commenter told Visual Basic-era readers to check out GAMBAS.

evidence_sources.author: d3Xt3r
evidence_sources.excerpt: for the slightly younger folks who have more memories of Visual Basic than QBasic, check out GAMBAS

items.name: pi-task-compaction
items.summary: A Pi extension that replaces completed task regions with model-generated summaries.
items.why_included: Its author reported strong compaction results in long real-world sessions.
items.evidence: The author said the summaries had been sufficient in practice and long sessions ended near 6% context use.

evidence_sources.author: spott
evidence_sources.excerpt: in practice the summaries have been good enough it hasn’t needed to. I’ve been using it with 5.6 sol, and even really long sessions have like 6% context used at the end.

items.name: explain-diff
items.summary: A skill that turns code diffs into explanatory documentation.
items.why_included: A user reported liking it in their personal software workflow and explicitly recommended trying it.
items.evidence: One commenter said they were using explain-diff, liked it, and recommended at least trying it.

evidence_sources.author: dtkav
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using Geoffrey's /explain-diff skill in my replace-github-with-tailor-fit-personal-software journey, and I'm liking it. I recommend at least giving it a try.

items.name: Sentry
items.summary: An application monitoring platform that tracks errors by software version.
items.why_included: A commenter found version-linked error context very useful for identifying root causes.
items.evidence: One commenter said Sentry's commit context made root-cause analysis much easier.

evidence_sources.author: bquaresma
evidence_sources.excerpt: Sentry being one of them, and I've found it very useful when those errors include context about which commit introduced the issue.

items.name: Psychological Warfare in Reverse Engineering
items.summary: A Black Hat talk on reverse engineering by hardware hacker Christopher Domas.
items.why_included: A commenter praised Domas as an exceptional explainer and named this among their favorite talks.
items.evidence: One commenter called Christopher Domas a favorite hacker and highlighted this as one of his favorite talks.

evidence_sources.author: MattSteelblade
evidence_sources.excerpt: Christopher Domas is one of my absolute favorite all-time hackers. He does such a fantastic job of explaining his work. Some of my favorite talks of his: - Psychological Warfare in Reverse Engineering
